title: Lakers to host LeBron James and 76ers in 2026 NBA Christmas Day matchup
text:
Lakers to host LeBron James and 76ers in 2026 NBA Christmas Day matchup
The Los Angeles Lakers will host LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers as part of the NBA’s five-game Christmas Day slate, the league announced early Tuesday morning on Aug. 11. James will return to Los Angeles for the first time since leaving the Lakers for the 76ers in free agency at age 41.
This marks the Lakers’ 28th consecutive season playing on Christmas Day, a streak dating back to 1999. During his tenure with the Lakers, James played in eight Christmas Day games, achieving a record of three wins and five losses. This year’s contest will be James’ twentieth consecutive appearance on Christmas Day and his twenty-first overall, with an overall holiday record of eleven wins and nine losses.
The matchup is considered one of the most anticipated games of this year’s schedule due to both teams' high-profile rosters. The Luka Doncic-led Lakers facing off against James on another major market team is expected to draw significant attention during the holiday.
Reports indicate that there was a mutual parting between James and the Lakers this offseason, with little animosity between both parties. However, how fans in Los Angeles receive James upon his return remains an open question after eight years with the franchise—a period that included bringing them back into championship contention and winning an NBA title in 2020.
The game between the Lakers and Sixers is scheduled for a 2:00 p.m. PT tip-off at Crypto.com Arena, airing on ESPN and ABC as part of what is widely regarded as primetime for NBA Christmas matchups. The day also features an NBA Finals rematch between San Antonio Spurs and New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden starting at 9:00 a.m. PT, along with Miami Heat vs. Boston Celtics (11:30 a.m.), Oklahoma City Thunder vs. Minnesota Timberwolves (5:00 p.m.), and Denver Nuggets vs. Golden State Warriors (7:30 p.m.). All games will be simulcast on ABC and ESPN.
